description: A local Python demo simulating a law firm's secure AI platform — ethical walls (case isolation), Entra ID-style login + MFA, RBAC, audit logging, and cost tracking, all mapped to real Azure/Microsoft cloud equivalents.
readme_excerpt:
# 🏛️ Law Firm AI Platform — Local Practice Project

**Your role:** AI Systems Administrator
**What it does:** Lets 3 lawyers safely use AI on 3 separate secret cases — and stops anyone from seeing another case's files (ethical walls).

| Lawyer | Login | Case | Defends |
|--------|-------|------|---------|
| 👩 Sarah | `sarah` | 💊 Medical | Drug company |
| 👨 David | `david` | 🏭 Manufacturing | Machine maker |
| 👩 Maria | `maria` | 🚬 Tobacco | Cigarette company |

Password for all: `demo123` · MFA codes: Sarah `111111`, David `222222`, Maria `333333`

---

## ▶️ How to run it

```bash
cd law-firm-ai-project
python3 app.py
```

It works **with no signup** (offline demo mode).
To get **real AI answers** with your OpenAI key, run this first (paste YOUR key):

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-your-key-here"
python3 app.py
```

⚠️ Your key stays on your Mac. Never put it in any file you share.

---

## 🔑 THE BIG COMPARISON — Local (this Mac) vs. Real Cloud (the job)

This is the most important part. Each piece of this project **pretends** to be a real
Microsoft cloud tool. Here is exactly what each one maps to:

| # | What you do here (LOCAL 💻) | In the file/code | What it would REALLY be (CLOUD ☁️) |
|---|------------------------------|------------------|-------------------------------------|
| 1 | Log in with username | `users.json` | **Microsoft Entra ID** (identity system) |
| 2 | Enter the 6-digit code | `mfa_code` check | **Entra ID MFA** (real phone code) |
| 3 | Group decides your access | `access.json` | **Azure RBAC** (role assignments) |
| 4 | You can only open your case | the access check | **Ethical walls** (SharePoint permissions) |
| 5 | Secret case files in folders | `cases/` | **SharePoint / iManage** (document system) |
| 6 | The AI answers questions | `call_ai()` (OpenAI) | **OpenAI GPT (gpt-4o-mini) / Azure OpenAI** |
| 7 | Connect AI to documents | code passes docs in | **APIs + Power Automate connectors** |
| 8 | Cost saved to a file | `cost_report.txt` | **Azure Cost Management** (dashboard) |
| 9 | Who-did-what saved to a file | `audit_log.txt` | **Azure Monitor / Entra Audit Logs** |
| 10 | Problems saved as tickets | `tickets/` | **ServiceNow / Jira** (help desk) |
| 11 | Admin resolves a ticket | `resolve_ticket()` | **ServiceNow / Jira** "Resolve" button |
| 12 | Ticket auto-checked, else a human reviews | `verify_ticket()` | **ServiceNow / Jira** triage automation + human review |

> **The IDEA is identical. Only the SIZE and the REAL TOOLS differ.**
> Local = a free practice "dollhouse." Cloud = the giant live version a company pays for.

---

description: Automated Microsoft Purview eDiscovery Premium legal hold export via the Graph API
readme_excerpt:
# Purview eDiscovery Export Automation

End-to-end automation of Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium) legal hold exports via the
Microsoft Graph API — built to export a multi-terabyte legal hold estate from a tenant
scheduled for decommission, without the legal team ever touching the Purview portal.

The workflow is fully scripted because the requirement was **defensibility**: attorneys
specify which custodians to export and in what order, and everything else — case discovery,
data source resolution, search scoping, collection, export, and download — happens the same
way every time, with a log and resumable state.

```
case → custodian (or non-custodial data source) → user source → review set
     → search → estimate → add to review set → export → download
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **Scale** | ~800 custodians and ~800 sites, roughly 22 TB / 66 million items |
| **API** | Microsoft Graph v1.0 `security/cases/ediscoveryCases` |
| **Auth** | Microsoft Graph SDK, plus MSAL.PS for the separate export download token |
| **Runtime per custodian** | 5 to 12+ hours, server-side, resumable |

---

## The three problems worth reading the code for

### 1. Multi-hour server-side jobs, and a client that cannot be trusted to survive them

`addToReviewSet` is the collection step, and it is slow. Measured durations on a real
tenant: **317 minutes, 530 minutes, 650 minutes, and one run over 12 hours.** The job runs
server-side, which is the important property — it survives the client dying.

The script is built around that fact. Two JSON state files are written per custodian:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `addToReviewSet-state.json` | Records the server-side operation ID. A re-run resumes *monitoring* an in-flight collection instead of starting a second one. |
| `export-state.json` | Records that collection finished and export was requested. A re-run skips straight to downloading, bypassing a multi-hour re-collection. Deleted only after every file has downloaded successfully. |

The script can be killed, the machine rebooted, and the next run picks up where it left off.
This has been exercised in both directions in production — after a deliberate stop, and
after a genuine collection timeout — with no data re-collected and nothing lost.

The collection timeout is set to **24 hours** (`$maxAddWaitMinutes = 1440`). It started at
two hours. Every increase came from a real job that outlived the previous value.

> **`addToReviewSet` reports 0% for its entire run**, then flips to 100% on completion.
> It is not a progress bar. Do not kill a job because it appears stuck — this cost real time
> to learn.

### 2. Mailboxes whose owning account no longer exists

is a large share of the s

description: Export Bitbucket, Confluence and Jira history as tamper-evident evidence — read-only, verbatim payloads, sha256-manifested JSONL. For tax audits, legal holds and e-discovery.
readme_excerpt:
# atlassian-evidence

**English** | [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md)

**Export the full history of Confluence, Jira and Bitbucket Cloud as tamper-evident
evidence** — strictly read-only, verbatim payloads, every batch sha256-manifested.

*Trích xuất toàn bộ lịch sử Confluence / Jira / Bitbucket Cloud thành bằng chứng có thể kiểm
chứng, phục vụ giải trình thuế, kiểm toán và tranh chấp pháp lý —*
[đọc bản tiếng Việt](README.vi.md).

---

## Is this your problem?

A tax authority, an auditor, or opposing counsel asks you to prove that **a specific thing
happened at a specific time** — and the evidence is scattered across years of Jira,
Confluence and Bitbucket:

- *"Prove this R&D project was actually carried out during fiscal year 2019."*
- *"Produce the complete discussion behind this decision — no excerpts."*
- *"This document says it was edited on 12 March. Where is the version before the edit?"*
- Employment disputes, IP ownership claims, or a departing employee who deleted or rewrote
  data on the way out.

It sounds simple until you try it.

### Why the built-in exports are not enough

| Approach | Why it fails as evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Jira XML/CSV export | Drops changelog, worklogs, comments; reformats timestamps |
| Confluence PDF/Word export | Current version only — version history is what matters |
| Screenshots | Unverifiable, trivially challenged as edited |
| A repo you already cloned locally | Unpushed local commits contaminate the evidence |
| Atlassian full-site backup | Opaque format; you cannot verify or produce any single item from it |

The core problem: evidence must be **provably unaltered** and **verbatim** — not "data that a
tool has reinterpreted for you".

### How this tool solves it

- **Read-only, enforced structurally.** The HTTP client exposes exactly one method, `.get()` —
  POST/PUT/DELETE do not exist anywhere in the code. Git is restricted to `clone --mirror`,
  `fetch --prune` and `log`. There is no code path that can write back to the source systems.
- **Absolutely verbatim.** Raw API payloads are preserved in each record's `raw` field. Every
  timestamp is stored as **the exact string the source returned** and is never parsed into a
  `datetime` and re-formatted — that silently rewrites timezone and millisecond precision.
- **Verifiable.** Each closed JSONL batch is hashed into `manifest.jsonl`. Re-run `sha256sum`
  at any point to prove a file has not changed since extraction.
- **Complete history.** Confluence captures **every version** of every page, not just the
  latest. Jira captures issues plus comments, changelogs and worklogs. Bitbucket captures
  commits (both `author_date` and `committer_date`, read from git itself) and pull requests in
  every state.
- **Transparent scope.** Each run writes a scope report
